name: Docker
description: Docker provides developer tools for building, sharing, and running containerized applications, including Docker Desktop, Docker Engine and CLI tooling, Docker Compose, Docker Hub, build services, and software-supply-chain features.
best_for: Best suited to developers and engineering teams that need a standardized container workflow across local development, CI, image distribution, and deployment environments.
features: Docker Desktop with Docker Engine, CLI, GUI, and local container workflows
Docker Compose for defining and running multi-container applications
Docker Hub for public and private image distribution
Docker Build and optional cloud build capacity
Docker Hardened Images and enterprise security controls on higher tiers

alternatives.name: Render
alternatives.description: A managed application-hosting platform that can deploy web services, workers, and databases without requiring you to operate a container platform yourself.
alternatives.best_for: Teams whose real goal is managed application deployment rather than replacing Docker with another container engine.

alternatives.name: Vercel
alternatives.description: A managed deployment platform for web and AI applications with Git-connected previews, global delivery, and managed compute.
alternatives.best_for: Web teams that want managed deployment and delivery instead of owning the underlying container workflow.

pricing.starting_price: $11/user/month for Pro on monthly billing; $9/user/month billed annually

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.notes: Free for eligible individual, education, open-source, and small-business use; Docker Desktop commercial-use licensing limits still apply.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.notes: $24/user/month billed annually; no monthly self-service price is listed.

cons: Docker Desktop commercial use at organizations with more than 250 employees OR more than $10 million in annual revenue requires a paid subscription.
Pro and Team are priced per user, and Business is $24/user/month on annual billing, so team cost scales with seats.
Cloud build, test, registry, and security features have plan-specific usage allowances; subscription price is not always the complete operating cost.

faq.question: Is Docker free for commercial use?
faq.answer: Docker Engine remains open source, but Docker Desktop has commercial-use licensing rules. Docker states that companies with more than 250 employees OR more than $10 million in annual revenue need a paid Pro, Team, or Business subscription for Docker Desktop.

faq.question: How much do Docker paid plans cost?
faq.answer: Docker Pro is $11 per user per month on monthly billing or $9 billed annually. Team is $16 monthly or $15 billed annually. Business is $24 per user per month on annual billing.

faq.question: Are Render and Vercel direct Docker replacements?
faq.answer: No. They are managed deployment alternatives for teams whose goal is to deploy applications without operating the same container workflow. They are not drop-in replacements for Docker Engine or Docker-compatible tooling.

faq.question: What should I inventory before moving away from Docker?
faq.answer: Inventory Dockerfiles, Compose files, image registries, base images, build pipelines, secrets, volumes, networking, local-development dependencies, and production runtime assumptions before choosing a replacement workflow.
